Where it began

Washington Sundar was born in Chennai on 5 October 1999 and had a bat in his hands by the age of four or five. Cricket ran in the house. His father, Mani Sundar, was a keen player who came close to a place in the Tamil Nadu side, and his sister Shailaja is a professional cricketer too. His unusual first name honours P. D. Washington, a former army man who had stood behind his father during his own playing days.

His schooling was at St. Bede's in Chennai, and he later took a degree in the city. He played for India at the 2016 Under-19 World Cup, and in October of that year he first played first-class cricket for Tamil Nadu. Like Ravichandran Ashwin before him, he started out as a batter and found his name as an off-spinner.

The player

His Test debut was one nobody had planned. He went to Australia in 2020–21 as a net bowler, but with others hurt and no easy way to fly replacements in, he was handed a cap for the final Test, at Brisbane. Steve Smith was his first Test wicket. Then he made 62 in his first innings and shared a stand of 123 for the seventh wicket with Shardul Thakur, which helped India to a famous win.

From 2021 to 2026 he played 18 Tests. He made 937 runs at 44.62, with a highest score of 101 not out, and took 41 wickets at 30.34. His best innings return was 7 for 59, and in October 2024 he took ten in a match against New Zealand. His first Test hundred came against England in 2025.

What made him special

He offered two jobs for the price of one. He bowled tight, thoughtful off-spin and batted left-handed with a calm that suited any situation. In white-ball cricket he made his name by bowling in the powerplay, the overs when most spinners would rather be somewhere else.

If there was one thing left to tidy, it was turning good starts into big scores. He passed fifty six times and went on to a hundred only once, though an average of 44.62 suggests the bowlers were rarely glad to see him.

Away from the middle

He became the youngest man to play a Twenty20 international for India, at 18, and in 2018 was Player of the Series in the Nidahas Trophy. He was in the Indian squads that won the 2023 Asia Cup, the Champions Trophy in 2025 and the T20 World Cup in 2026. In the Indian Premier League he played for several sides, and in 2022 he had a spell with Lancashire, taking five wickets in an innings on his debut.

And finally

Few players can say they turned up to bowl in the nets and left with a Test cap, a first wicket of Steve Smith and a share in a winning Test. It was quite a promotion for someone who had packed for practice.
